unit: whichever is less, from the property line
qualifier: Fort Lauderdale caps a dock at 25% of the waterway's width or 25 ft from the property line, whichever is less. Mooring piles may reach 30% or 25 ft, and the boat itself must stay inside the house's side setback lines extended into the water. Only the City Commission can go further, and never past 30% of the width.

headline_answer: No fixed size limit; 4 ft depth rule
unit: dock must link to a channel at least 4 ft deep at mean low water
qualifier: Key West's land development regulations set no length, width or side setback for a private dock. What they do require is depth: a dock, pier or wharf is allowed only where a continuous channel at least 4 ft deep at mean low water links it to deep water, and only with Army Corps approval. In the Conservation district, whose areas include waters reaching 600 ft into the tidal water next to the city limits, docks are a conditional use and may be no wider than 5 ft.

On regulated waterways other than the Intracoastal, a dock may reach no more than 25 ft or 25% of the waterway width, whichever is less, and the seawall cap and dock together may be no more than 8 ft wide. Single-family docks keep a 25 ft side setback (15 ft on lots 50 to 70 ft wide).
